A dispatch (or expo) station follows each order from the moment it is sent and acts only when the whole order is ready. With a driver step, it also records who took a delivery out."}},{"node":"markdown102","element":"markdown","data":{"label":"Set it up","key":"md_set_it_up","id":"set-it-up","name":"md_set_it_up","value":"# Set it up

1. Create a production center, for example *Dispatch*, with the **Item Groups** of everything it hands out (usually all of them, or the parent group).
2. Turn on **Wait for the whole order**.
3. Give it a flow that starts where the kitchen ends, for example *Completed → On the way → Delivered*.
4. The status *On the way* has **Ask who delivers** on ([Order statuses](/Docs/Order%20Statuses)).
5. To use it only for deliveries, turn on **Only these tables** and choose the *Delivery* table.
6. Give the drivers a role with **Delivers orders** (the *Driver* role has it) and give them the dispatch station in [Ren Staff](/Docs/Staff%20and%20Roles)."}},{"node":"markdown103","element":"markdown","data":{"label":"Working it","key":"md_working_it","id":"working-it","name":"md_working_it","value":"# Working it

- Each order appears as soon as it is sent, with every item and *Waiting for the kitchen · 2 of 3 ready*. Items still being prepared look dimmed.
- When everything is ready the button works: **Dispatch** asks **Who delivers it?**: pick a driver from the list, or type another name.
- The order banner on the POS shows *On the way with Diego*; the delivery time and the address are on the ticket.
- **Deliver** when it arrives marks the order delivered. The order is then charged as usual (cash on delivery is recorded by the cashier or the driver if they charge).

Items no station prepares (a canned soda) don't hold the order: they count as ready and go out with it."}}]}]
